To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) discourse cues are anchored on trees in a Tree-Adjoining grammar; (2) this anchoring is realized by a set of operations that adjoin to trees and are triggered by cue phrases; (3) these operations include a set of basic operations that are used to construct the discourse structure, and a set of operations for presupposition that are used to enrich discourse semantics; and (4) the resulting discourse structure can be used to derive discourse semantics.
(1) discourse cues can be anchored to trees in a lexicalized TALG and (2) this approach can account for the different discourse cue patterns in the data.

the discourse of a text can be modeled as a sequence of discourse trees anchored on cue phrases, and that this sequence can be generated by the application of discourse tree operations to the discourse trees.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) the nature of the basic discourse units, and how they relate to the units of sentence grammar; (2) the nature and role of discourse cues, and how they are related to the basic discourse units; and (3), how discourse semantics is related to sentence semantics.
the question of how the meaning of discourse is composed from its elements, and we have found that a lexicalized TAG provides a useful tool for exploring this question.

the following questions. How can discourse cues be used to anchor larger discourse units? How can the resulting grammar be lexicalized? What are the sources for discourse meaning, and how do they interact?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lexicalized TAG for discourse we present is a promising first step towards the goal of developing a fully lexicalized TAG for the analysis and generation of discourse, but much work remains.

a lexicalized TAL grammar for discourse is a promising approach that has a number of advantages over other approaches, and that is capable of accounting for a wide variety of phenomena, but that there are still many open questions.

a lexicalized TAG for discourse can account for a wide range of discourse cues in terms of their contribution to discourse structure, and that this account is consistent with a compositional semantics, but that it also allows for a presuppositional and inferential semantics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a formalism and a computational implementation for discourse that can handle the three sources of discourse meaning, and we have shown that the formalism is powerful enough to capture many of the phenomena of discourse, and that it can be implemented to produce coherent, plausible discourse.
we have shown that a fully lexicalized TAG for discourse can be developed and that it can account for a wide variety of data.

we have developed a formalism for representing discourse structure that is based on a lexicalized Tree-Adjioning Grammar, and we have developed an algorithm for parsing discourse structure using this grammar.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a discourse grammar that takes the basic building blocks to be anchored on discourse cues, and that allows the discourse cues to freely adjoin to the basic trees, provides a simple account for a range of phenomena that are otherwise difficult to capture in a lexicalized TAG.
the same lexicalized tree-adjoining grammar that is used to describe intra-sentential phenomena can be used to describe discourse phenomena.

the discourse grammar can be made to look very much like the grammar of the sentences it embeds, with the same basic operations and structures, and that the discourse grammar has the same compositional semantics as the grammar of the sentence.
